identity.title: VLA and ALMA observations of the lensed radio-quiet quasar SDSS J0924+0219: a molecular structure in a 3 μJy radio source
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) and Atacama Large Millimetre Array (ALMA) observations of SDSS J0924+0219, a _z_ =1.524 radio-quiet lensed quasar with an intrinsic radio flux density of about 3 µJy.

evidence.quote: SDSS J0924+0219 was discovered by Inada et al. (2003) as part of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey Quasar Lens Search (SQLS) and consists of a radio-quiet quasar at z = 1.524 quadruply imaged by an early-type galaxy at z = 0.394 (Eigenbrod et al. 2006).

Where necessary we assume a flat Universe with H 0 = 68.3 km s [−][1] Mpc [−][1] and Ω m = 0.3; for the source this gives a luminosity distance D L = 11400 Mpc and an angular size distance D A = 1790 Mpc.

question.value: What are the properties of the radio and molecular gas reservoirs in the lensed radio-quiet quasar SDSS J0924+0219, and what causes its optical flux ratio anomaly?

evidence.quote: We observed SDSS J0924+0219 in order to investigate the properties of the radio and molecular gas reservoirs in the source, and investigate the causes of the flux anomaly further.
What is the size of the radio-emitting region, what physical processes produce it, and is it co-spatial with the molecular line gas?
Is the optical flux anomaly due to microlensing?
Project code 2018.1.01447.S

claims.hypothesis: The weak radio emission in the radio-quiet lensed quasar SDSS J0924+0219 originates from an extended star-forming region co-spatial with the molecular gas reservoir rather than a compact point source.
claims.experiment: Observed SDSS J0924+0219 with VLA at 5.5 GHz and ALMA in CO(5-4), compared convolved maps, fitted point-source and extended source lens models in the image and u-v planes, and calculated the radio-FIR correlation parameter q_IR.
claims.result: Point-source models leave severe over/under-subtraction residuals; u-v lens modelling yields intrinsic FWHMs of 0.081 +/- 0.008 arcsec for CO(5-4) and 0.120 +/- 0.089 arcsec for radio at consistent positions, and q_IR = 2.35 lies within the standard radio-FIR correlation (2.40 +/- 0.24).
claims.finding: The radio emission is inconsistent with a point source and is consistent with being co-spatial with the ~1-2.5 kpc rotating molecular disk, naturally explained by star formation.

evidence.quote: Our results are consistent with the radio emission being emitted from the same region, but not with a point source of radio emission.

evidence.loc: 4.1 The radio source and the CO(5-4) line
evidence.quote: Combining the radio flux density from this work with the previously determined far-IR flux densities of Stacey et al. (2018), it appears that SDSS J0924+0219 lies on the standard radio-FIR correlation (Ivison et al. 2010); the corresponding q IR parameter is found to be 2.35, well within the range of q IR = 2.40 ± 0.24 found by Ivison et al. (2010).

claims.hypothesis: The CO(5-4) molecular gas in SDSS J0924+0219 resides in a structure with ordered velocity motion such as a rotating molecular disk.
claims.experiment: Sliced the ALMA CO(5-4) cube by frequency and projected each velocity channel back to the source plane using an SIE lens model with a single elliptical Gaussian source per channel.
claims.result: The reconstructed source centroids form a roughly linear sequence from red to blue velocities (~50-100 km/s) across 0.1-0.3 arcsec (~850-2500 pc).
claims.finding: The molecular gas displays ordered motion consistent with a rotating molecular disk of 1-2.5 kpc extent, though higher resolution and sensitivity are needed to confirm detailed disk kinematics.

evidence.quote: The molecular gas displays ordered motion, in a structure approximately 1–2.5 kpc in physical extent, with typical velocities of 50-100 km s [−][1] .

evidence.loc: 3.1.2 ALMA observations: velocity-resolved structure in the CO(5-4) line
evidence.quote: Given the limited angular resolution, the structure could be consistent with a rotating molecular disk (eg Smit et al. 2018), which has a size of between 0 [′′] . 1 and 0 [′′] . 3 depending on the exact centroids inferred for the lower-frequency parts of the source, corresponding to ∼ 850–2500 pc at the redshift of this quasar.

claims.hypothesis: The extreme (~12:1) and long-lived (15-year) optical flux ratio anomaly between merging images A and D is caused by stellar microlensing rather than dark matter substructure millilensing.
claims.experiment: Measured the A/D flux ratio in the radio and CO(5-4) line, fitted smooth SIE lens models including a substructure anomaly parameter f_AD, and simulated a microlensing magnification map for image D using Wambsganss (2001) ray-tracing code.
claims.result: The A/D flux ratio is 1.28 +/- 0.41 in the radio and 1.58 +/- 0.15 in CO(5-4); smooth SIE lens models with an extended source yield f_AD = 1 (CO) and 0.97 (radio); microlensing simulations show demagnification regions of factor >= 12 lasting 20 to 60 years.
claims.finding: No millilensing perturbation by dark matter substructure is required; the slight radio/CO departure from 1 is explained by the extended source size, and the 15-year optical anomaly is plausibly caused by stellar microlensing.

evidence.quote: The observation that f AD = 1 implies that the SIE model we used clearly reproduces the main features of the data and is compatible with an extended source, together with no requirement for additional perturbations due to millilensing by substructure.

evidence.loc: 4.2 Is microlensing the reason behind the optical flux ratio anomaly?
evidence.quote: Figure 16 shows a fraction of this map where multiple regions demagnified by at least a factor 12 are observed. Those regions extend over several η 0, which translates to periods of demagnification that can last over 20 to 60 years.

why_this_data.value: SDSS J0924+0219 has an extreme 12:1 optical flux anomaly persisting for 15 years; longer-wavelength radio and submm/CO observations probe source sizes >> 1 uas that are immune to microlensing, while also tracing the star-forming molecular gas and radio continuum.

evidence.quote: Measurements at longer wavelengths, where the continuum source size is ≫ 1µas and not subject to microlensing, are important
We observed SDSS J0924+0219 in order to investigate the properties of the radio and molecular gas reservoirs in the source, and investigate the causes of the flux anomaly further.

why_this_method.value: Initial image-plane modelling provides easy visual assessment and necessary starting parameters for convergence in u-v plane fitting (uvmultifit and visilens); low SNR and resolution motivated simple parametric Gaussian/Sersic source models rather than pixelized source reconstruction or u-v channel modelling.

evidence.quote: We describe both phases of this process, firstly because the initial starting model is typically necessary to get good convergence in the u − v fitting part of the process, and because it allows easy visual assessment of the fits.

referee_caveats_inferred: The ALMA observation is a very short (5 min on-source) compact-configuration snapshot with ~0.6-0.8 arcsec resolution, which only marginally resolves the individual lensed images (~0.5-1.8 arcsec separation).

The u-v visibility fits with uvmultifit have high reduced chi-squared values before weight rescaling (4.68 for CO, 11.24 for radio), and the radio fit required forcing all four images to share a single width and axis ratio to converge.
The dynamical mass estimate assumes an inclined rotating disk with radius equal to half the Sersic/Gaussian FWHM, which is poorly constrained at this angular resolution.
